algorithm: Enumerate zero to two coins of each small denomination and derive the minimum number of threes needed to represent every price.
correctness_argument: Three or more ones can be replaced by fewer coins of denominations one and two without losing any subset sum; three twos can be replaced by one two, one one and one three while preserving their subset sums and coin count, and further normalized. Therefore an optimum exists with at most two ones and two twos. For each such choice enumerate their usage and maximize the per-price minimum count of threes.
problem_understanding: Normalize the inventory to at most two coins of each small denomination.

steps.claim: Implementation follows these obligations: Normalize the inventory to at most two coins of each small denomination. Enumerate the small-coin inventory. For each price enumerate all available small-coin subsets. A nonnegative remainder divisible by three determines the needed threes. The maximum per-price need suffices because only one flavor is purchased.
